Forest: Roots run in rings too even for a tree that was only growing.
A cornered wolf still hesitates at a raised hand, then remembers its teeth.
Bark is carved one mark over another, past any one knife's patience.
Moss holds the rings of old fire pits, cold now, banked and left.
A hush moves here that the wind did not start and cannot finish.
Iron under the leaf refuses to rust the way tired iron should.
Fire pits sit in rings too neat for one cook and one night.
The canopy keeps a dark that does not match the hour beyond it.
Tracks cross the mold and stop, as if the walker were taken mid-stride.
Lava: Heat comes off the stone thick enough to taste at the back of the throat.
Cracks breathe a slow orange, in time with whatever shifts beneath.
The air bends torchlight and does not give it back straight.
Metal has run and pooled into shapes no tool ever asked for.
Ash falls fine as snow and does not care what it buries.
Rock stays warm where no flame has any business remaining.
Steam lifts a smell of scorched iron from cracks too thin to see.
Deep in the stone the heat is being fed, and the feeding has not stopped.
Crypt: Names are cut into the wall faster than any mourner meant to cut them.
The air in here has quit moving, and the rest of the world can keep its wind.
Dust lies so even it looks placed, and it does not care whose face it covers.
Bones rest in rows a restless dead would never have kept so neat.
Cold sits in the stone, lets a torch pretend, then takes the warmth back.
Faded gifts line the low shelves, left by hands that did not stay to be thanked.
A deep door has been sealed so long the dust on it has grown its own dust.
The silence here is not empty. It is kept, and the keeping has a preference.
Crystal: Light moves in the walls on a pulse the room did not learn from any heart.
Crystal grows in layers too even to shrug off as chance.
Stand still and the stone hums back, faint, like an answer to a question.
Every face throws the torch off at an angle the room does not own.
Warmth and cold trade places in the stone, and nobody has mapped the trade.
Shards on the floor could open a hand, and nothing looks freshly broken.
The formations lean inward, all of them, toward a center they agree on.
Something under the crystal is feeding it, and the feed has not run out.
Temple: Steps wear up toward an altar whose job outlived the hands that knew it.
Incense still clings to the stone, faint, and refuses to finish leaving.
Carvings cover the walls for a worship that no longer signs its work.
A gap in the roof puts light on one tile and does it without being asked.
Gifts sit at the altar's foot, untouched, still waiting on a hand.
The quiet is held on purpose. Mere emptiness would be louder.
Every line of the stone draws the eye to the center, and the center knows.
This place was built to be found. The finding is the part still open.
Cavern: Water drips on a count nobody is keeping, and the count does not slip.
Rock is cut in places too regular for water's patience alone.
Cold air moves from passages deeper than a torch can embarrass.
Columns stand where ceiling and floor met and then refused to part.
A metal glint shows where the rock wore thin, buried past an easy reach.
The dark has weight here. Bare skin can feel the press of it.
Echoes travel farther than honest stone allows, and they come back wrong.
A pale vein in the rock is warm under the hand, with no fire to blame.
Swamp: Water holds still and dark enough to hide a body that is standing in it.
Rot hangs sweet and close, and does not apologize for the sweetness.
Roots climb out of the mud in shapes that reach, which growth need not do.
Fog sits on the water and declines every invitation from the day.
Metal winks under the shallows, and the wink is not a fish.
The ground takes a foot deeper than the step agreed to go.
Unseen insects hold one note, and the note does not tire.
Timbers jut from the mud on lines too straight to be a tree that fell.
Desert: Heat makes the next ridge lie about how far away it really is.
Wind has scoured the ground down to things that were buried for a reason.
Thin metal juts from the dunes, half swallowed, worn past any tool's name.
Silence carries out here, broken only when the sand decides to settle.
Patches of ground have fused to glass under a heat no cookfire owns.
Bones bleach to one color, and the sun does not bother to sort them.
When the wind dies, something under the dunes hums and is not finished.
Sand holds a long hollow, larger than any walker, and the hollow is old.
Ice: Frost climbs in patterns too fine for weather to have drawn by itself.
The cold takes the bone first and lets the air catch up after.
Ice has sealed a shape into one wall, and the shape is not in a hurry.
Breath hangs and fades slower than the cold, alone, can explain.
The floor is ice that will hold a step and ice that wants to argue.
Wind finds cracks too thin to see and brings a sound like distant breath.
Something pale holds still under the sheet, waiting the cold out.
Frost swallows sound until the quiet sits on the room like a lid.
Ruins: Walls stand that used to be a whole, and the whole is not explaining itself.
Fallen columns lie half buried, their cuts worn past any sure reading.
Joints in this stone are tighter and cleaner than later work bothers to be.
Vines take almost everything, and a few surfaces refuse them outright.
The foundation hums, faint, and only if a body stands still enough to hear.
Rubble covers the floor except where it does not, and the exception is wide.
Lintels sit high for an easy reach, and they were cut to sit that high.
It was built to outlast its use, and the use is the part that lost.
Castle: Corridors of cold stone run longer than one plan would have dared.
Banners have faded past any mark still worth a name.
The keep is a stack of repairs, each one hiding a crack the last one missed.
Draft walks the halls from openings no mason meant to leave.
Iron gates hang rusted and propped, held by habit more than by a smith.
Soot climbs the walls in layers, each torch adding its own black.
The floor is walked smooth by feet that did not stay to be counted.
A bell hangs ready overhead and has not been given a reason to speak.
Graveyard: Headstones lean at angles the ground chose after the masons were done.
Grass grows thick on one plot and starves on the next, and will not explain.
The oldest markers are worn past reading, and fresh flowers sit by them anyway.
Fog takes the ground most mornings and gives it back late, if at all.
One tree stands bare when the rest is green, its roots deeper than the graves.
Flowers lie by markers whose names are gone, left by hands that came anyway.
The ground settles in lumps, and a careless step finds the hollow.
Crows keep this yard more faithfully than any visitor who still has a pulse.
Generic: Cut stone lines the walls, plain, old, and uninterested in being admired.
Dust owns the corners, and nobody has picked a fight with it lately.
The air holds still, neither warm nor cold, saving itself for what comes next.
Torch brackets march the wall at even gaps, and half of them are empty.
A scorch on one wall tells a short, hot story and then withholds the end.
The floor is worn by feet, and the feet did not stay to sign the work.
A draft arrives from nowhere a finger can point to, carrying only itself.
The room keeps its shape out of spite, worn thin and not yet willing to drop.

kitchen: Green wood smokes under a pot, and the fat in it has not been scraped.

chamber: Walls of root close this hollow to a throat, and sound dies before it leaves.

shrine: A stone sits among the roots, and the gifts at its foot are still damp.

armory: Blades are quenched in cracks of fire and come up the color of the pit.

library: Ledgers of the dead line a shelf, and the last page is newer than the rest.

catacomb: Passages of the dead run tighter than a living stride enjoys.

shrine: A small holy spot, tended harder than the hall that leads to it.

Ash, a marker, and a bargain that still seems to be in force.
laboratory: Alembics, residue, and a bench worked well past tidiness.

observatory: A slit in the roof keeps a strip of night, and the charts want that strip.

Someone was reading the dark from here and left between one mark and the next.
throne: The seat is the room. Everything else is only the approach.
